prompt:
Normalize the single contact block in the user's note. Emit only a bare JSON object with exactly the keys name, phone, email, company, country. Each value must be a string or JSON null.

Read the block, not the surrounding prose or signature. Recognize label/value lines with colon, equals or tab separators, allowing variable labels and order. Trim values and collapse whitespace runs to one space. Treat absent lines, empty values and the following whole-value placeholders as missing, ignoring case: -, --, n/a, na, none, unknown, ?, null, TBD. Missing means null, with only the country exception below. Do not derive fields from domains, suffixes or surrounding text.

Route values before changing their format. Any record value with @ goes to email. To identify phone, first strip a leading tel: and any trailing extension (ext. or ext followed by digits, x or # followed by digits, or extension followed by digits). The remaining candidate is a phone if it has at least seven digits and contains only digits, spaces, plus signs, hyphens, parentheses, dots or slashes. These content tests take priority over phone/email labels. Use the country line as the only explicit country source. For name and company, swap the labeled values if the name-labeled value ends with a legal suffix and the company-labeled value does not. The suffix list for both swapping and cleanup, ignoring case, is: AB, GmbH, AG, Ltd, Ltd., PLC, Inc, Inc., LLC, Corp, Corp., AS, ASA, Oy, Oyj, A/S, ApS, SA, SAS, B.V., N.V., S.p.A., Sp. z o.o., K.K., Pty Ltd, Ltda.

Resolve country and phone as follows:
- Convert the nonmissing country line to uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Accept English, Swedish and German country names, alpha-2 and alpha-3 codes in any case, and common aliases: UK and Great Britain → GB; Holland → NL; USA and U.S.A. → US; Türkiye → TR; Czech Republic → CZ.
- Check the phone prefix after removing tel: and the extension, ignoring an opening parenthesis. A prefix of + or 00 means international. Delete the optional trunk marker (0) and all spaces, hyphens, dots, slashes and parentheses; replace a leading 00 with +. Keep the written calling code regardless of the country line. Only when the country line is absent, empty or a placeholder, fill country from this calling code if it uniquely identifies a country. Shared codes, including +1 and +7, leave country null.
- Otherwise the phone is national. With a normalized country, remove formatting and one leading trunk 0, then prefix + and that country's calling code. Without a country, set a national phone to null. All retained phones are E.164: + followed by the calling code and national significant number, digits only after the plus.

Finish the text values:
- Name: at the first comma, move the text before the comma after the text following it. Drop leading Dr, Mr, Mrs, Ms, Mx, Prof, with optional dot and regardless of case. For every space- or hyphen-separated part, uppercase its first character and lowercase the rest.
- Company: remove its trailing legal suffix from the list above, including an optional preceding comma. Uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space-separated word.
- Email: strip surrounding angle brackets and the mailto: prefix, whether the prefix is inside or outside the brackets. Lowercase the entire address.

Trim the results and collapse any remaining whitespace runs. Keep Unicode letters and diacritics through casing; never transliterate. Strings are compared after NFC normalization. Do not add prose, Markdown, or keys.
